why: I checked both verifier checks against their expect lines. Check 1's PASS condition says the two outputs must be "deep-equal arrays" after both are parsed as JSON. That matches "prints the same JSON array" and doesn't require byte-identical output. Its FAIL condition covers only a command error, output that isn't a JSON array, or arrays that differ. Running several tables is fine because the words say "the same table", which means any table. Check 2 passes if README.md "mentions the --tsv flag and says what it does". That's a fair reading of "documents --tsv", since documenting a flag means explaining it, and it asks for no exact wording. The stricter tests are all listed under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)": running npm test, whether a --tsv test was added, byte-identical diff output including the trailing newline, and unchanged plain CSV behaviour. No PASS or FAIL condition asks for more than its expect line's words.
